To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

organizational readiness is a multi-faceted construct that is a function of the perceived importance of the change and the collective appraisal of three key determinants (task demands, resource availability and situational factors).

organizational readiness for change can be defined as the shared resolve of organizational members to implement an organizational change and their shared belief in their capability to do so, and that organizational readiness for changes varies as a function how favorably organizational members appraise three key implementation capability determinants: task demands, resources available, and situational characteristics.

organizational readiness for change refers both to the degree of shared commitment among organizational members to implementing a change and to the degree of confidence in their collective capabilities to do so.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a theory of the antecedents and consequences of organizational readiness for planned change.
the question of whether and how the implementation of evidence based practice can be improved by focusing on organizational readiness for change.
the development of a theory of organizational readiness and its application to the field of healthcare management.

the theory described herein is an interesting and plausible way of conceptualizing organizational readiness for change, and that it is worth pursuing.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the theory is a useful way to conceptualize organizational readiness and to think about how it is created.
organizational readiness for change can be defined as an organization's shared belief that a change can be implemented successfully and that it is the right thing to do.
the theory of organizational readiness provides a conceptual framework for understanding how organizations can be prepared for change.
The main takeaway from our work is that
organizational readiness is an important construct for understanding and improving organizational change.
organizational readiness for change can be conceptualized as an organizational level construct, and its determinants and effects can be investigated using a variety of methodological designs.
organizational readiness for change should be considered an important outcome of organizational change efforts and not just a precursor to them.
